correctness.rationale: Four-point Lipschitz norm derived directly from all six metric constraints. Exact support function yields Q; independent sign-group averaging proves diagonal sufficiency. All vertices of positive orthant computed, then two global lower bounds proved with positive partial derivatives for t≤1 and convex KKT multipliers for t>1, each matched by a positive-definite ellipsoid. Endpoint t=1 and t=2 handled. Standalone standard-library verifier exactly reconstructs 48 rational vertex sets and verifies 2304 additional candidates, but continuum correctness rests on the analytic proof, not sampling.

value.rationale: Full metric-admissible parameter range for a canonical one-edge deformation of an equilateral four-point space, giving the precise phase change, uniquely most-Hilbertian equilateral member and endpoint behavior. Optimal Hilbertian distortion is a natural functional-analytic invariant not derivable from the source L1 classification, volume-product formulas, or isometry statements. A full three-dimensional constrained ellipsoid min–max proof is structurally nontrivial. The same branch threshold t=1 is independently motivated by Godard’s four-point tree condition: the three opposite-pair sums are t+1,2,2, and the metric is a tree metric exactly when t≤1; that historical qualitative result does not determine the sharp Euclidean distortion.
